<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="סיון_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518918811_theRebbe_734" batchId="meluket-_D7_A1_D7_99_D7_95_D7_9F_meluket__BH_POST_1766518918811_theRebbe_734__p004">
  <section v="9">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that Yehudah's offering first is linked to the quality of action, because nullification (bittul) is most complete in the power of action, which lacks the inherent superiority of higher faculties.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">6)</t>
    <t s="1">And we must connect this explanation</t>
    <t s="2">[that Yehudah offered first is due to the superiority of action]</t>
    <t s="3">with the explanation</t>
    <t s="4">(brought above in section 2)</t>
    <t s="5">that Yehudah offered first because Yehudah is the aspect of bittul (self-nullification),</t>
    <t s="6">for the concept of bittul is in action.</t>
    <t s="7">For the powers that are above action,</t>
    <t s="8">since their essence is superiority and perfection,</t>
    <t s="9">as explained above</t>
    <t s="10">(section 5)</t>
    <t s="11">that the beginning of man's superiority is the power of speech within him,</t>
    <t s="12">their bittul to the soul is not complete bittul,</t>
    <t s="13">and specifically the power of action, which is not from man's superiority,</t>
    <t s="14">its bittul to the soul is complete bittul.</t>
    <t s="15">[And in action itself,</t>
    <t s="16">the essence of bittul is in the level of action as it is separate from the powers above it.</t>
    <t s="17">For in the level of action in which the powers above it are clothed,</t>
    <t s="18">there is the elevation that through it the hidden aspect of the soul is revealed,</t>
    <t s="19">and therefore it is "existence."</t>
    <t s="20">And the essence of bittul is in the action itself</t>
    <t s="21">(which is separate from the powers above it),</t>
    <t s="22">for since it has no elevation,</t>
    <t s="23">therefore it is felt in it that all its existence is only from the soul.]</t>
  </section>
  <section v="10">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section connects the above to the idea that the root of action is in the essence of the soul, and likewise above, the essence of mitzvos is in Atzmus, so bittul is primarily in the action of mitzvos, revealing this truth also in Torah.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And we must connect this with the fact that the root of action is in the essence of the soul,</t>
    <t s="1">for in the essence of the soul there is no place for existence outside the soul.</t>
    <t s="2">And from this it is understood,</t>
    <t s="3">that the root of action being in the essence of the soul is because all its existence is only from the essence of the soul.</t>
    <t s="4">And likewise above</t>
    <t s="5">(in the distinction between Torah and mitzvos),</t>
    <t s="6">that the will for mitzvos is in the action of the mitzvos</t>
    <t s="7">(and in physical things),</t>
    <t s="8">even though action has no value,</t>
    <t s="9">it is because the root of mitzvos is in Atzmus,</t>
    <t s="10">and therefore,</t>
    <t s="11">the essence of bittul is in the action of the mitzvos.</t>
    <t s="12">And it can be said,</t>
    <t s="13">that also the will for the intention of the mitzvos,</t>
    <t s="14">is not due to the superiority of the intention of the mitzvos, but because it arose in His will, blessed be He.</t>
    <t s="15">However, the revelation of this matter is in the action of the mitzvos,</t>
    <t s="16">and through this it is revealed that it is so also in the intention of the mitzvos.</t>
    <t s="17">And likewise in Torah,</t>
    <t s="18">that although Torah is wisdom</t>
    <t s="19">[and also above,</t>
    <t s="20">Torah is the wisdom of the Holy One, blessed be He],</t>
    <t s="21">that "the Torah and the Holy One, blessed be He, are entirely one" is not due to the superiority of Torah, but because it arose in His will, blessed be He.</t>
    <t s="22">However, the revelation of this matter is in the mitzvos, and through the mitzvos it is revealed that it is so also in Torah.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="11">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that on the second day, Nesanel ben Tzu'ar (from the root "tzar" meaning distress) drew the bittul of Yehudah into Torah study, and is therefore considered as if he offered first, bringing the bittul of the level of "beginning" into Chochmah.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">7)</t>
    <t s="1">And this is "On the second day, Nesanel ben Tzu'ar offered" — the term "Tzu'ar" [implies distress],</t>
    <t s="2">for after the bittul of Yehudah regarding the matter of mitzvos, Nesanel ben Tzu'ar drew this bittul also into the occupation with Torah.</t>
    <t s="3">And therefore Scripture considers him as if he offered first</t>
    <t s="4">[even though Yehudah is above Yissachar,</t>
    <t s="5">as explained above</t>
    <t s="6">(section 2)</t>
    <t s="7">that Yehudah is in Kesser and Yissachar is in Chochmah],</t>
    <t s="8">for the concept of "offered first" is that he drew the bittul of Kesser</t>
    <t s="9">(the aspect of "beginning")</t>
    <t s="10">into Chochmah.</t>
    <t s="11">And it can be said that in the phrase "as if he offered first"</t>
    <t s="12">(and not "as if he offered on the first day")</t>
    <t s="13">is also hinted the bittul from the aspect of "beginning" — the beginning that precedes the beginning of thought,</t>
    <t s="14">in which arose "the end of action"</t>
    <t s="15">(the action of mitzvos)</t>
    <t s="16">and Nesanel drew this bittul also into Torah.</t>
    <t s="17">[Also, it can be said that the meaning of "as if he offered first" is a beginning before Yehudah.</t>
    <t s="18">For the drawing of bittul into Torah is a greater innovation and consequently more elevated than the bittul in the action of mitzvos.]</t>
    <t s="19">And through the bittul of "Tzu'ar" that was in him, he became "Nesanel,"</t>
    <t s="20">the letters of "Nasan Kel" (God gave),</t>
    <t s="21">meaning that Torah was given to him as a gift.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
